DEFINITION · qeva:1:local-global@1

Local versus global optimum

A local optimum is best in a neighborhood; a global optimum is best over the entire feasible domain.

editorialoptimization · dynamics
Run a related experimentTrace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Being unbeatable nearby does not mean being best everywhere.

EXACT

The compact statement

For minimization, x* is a local minimizer if some neighborhood U satisfies f(x*)≤f(x) for all x∈U∩X. It is global if the inequality holds for all x∈X.

Example

f(x)=(x^2-1)^2+0.1x has distinct local minima of different objective values.

Boundary / caveat

Some problems have no local traps (for example certain convex problems), while others have many. The distinction depends on the feasible geometry and objective.

Assumptions

  • A feasible set, objective, and neighborhood structure are specified.
